```{r}
# install.packages(c("sf", "utils"))  # if needed
library(sf)

get_nyc_council_districts <- function(
  dest_dir = "data/mp03",
  include_water = FALSE,     # FALSE => clipped to shoreline (nycc); TRUE => water-included (nyccwi)
  simplify_tol_m = NULL      # e.g., 5 for ~5 meters; NULL to skip simplifying
) {
  dir.create(dest_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  # Pick edition + filename pattern from DCP metadata (25C is current as of 2025-08-18)
  edition <- "25c"
  base <- if (include_water) "nyccwi" else "nycc"
  zip_url <- sprintf("https://www.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/zip/data-maps/open-data/%s_%s.zip",
                     base, edition)

  zip_path <- file.path(dest_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.zip", base, edition))
  unz_dir  <- file.path(dest_dir, sprintf("%s_%s", base, edition))

  # i) & ii) Download only if needed
  if (!file.exists(zip_path)) {
    message("Downloading: ", zip_url)
    utils::download.file(zip_url, zip_path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  } else {
    message("ZIP already exists, not downloading again: ", zip_path)
  }

  # iii) Unzip only if needed
  if (!dir.exists(unz_dir)) {
    message("Unzipping to: ", unz_dir)
    utils::unzip(zip_path, exdir = unz_dir)
  } else {
    message("Unzipped folder already exists, reusing: ", unz_dir)
  }

  # Locate the .shp (handles either folder structure)
  shp <- list.files(unz_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
  if (length(shp) == 0) stop("No .shp found after unzip. Check ZIP contents.")
  shp <- shp[1]

  # iv) Read shapefile
  dat <- sf::st_read(shp, quiet = TRUE)

  # v) Transform to WGS84 (EPSG:4326)
  dat <- sf::st_transform(dat, crs = "WGS84")

  # Optional: simplify geometry to speed up plotting
  if (!is.null(simplify_tol_m)) {
    # st_simplify uses layer CRS units; after transform to WGS84, units are degrees.
    # Convert meters → degrees approximately using meters/111_320 (at NYC latitude).
    tol_deg <- simplify_tol_m / 111320
    dat$geometry <- sf::st_simplify(dat$geometry, dTolerance = tol_deg, preserveTopology = TRUE)
  }

  dat
}

```
```{r}
# Clipped-to-shoreline version (good for most maps)
council <- get_nyc_council_districts()

# Water-included legal boundary
council_wi <- get_nyc_council_districts(include_water = TRUE)

# If plotting feels slow, simplify ~5 meters (visually lossless for citywide maps)
council_fast <- get_nyc_council_districts(simplify_tol_m = 5)
```

```{r}
# install.packages(c("httr2", "sf", "dplyr", "purrr", "glue"))  # if needed
library(httr2)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(glue)

get_nyc_tree_points <- function(
  dest_dir = "data/mp03",
  base_id  = "uvpi-gqnh",      # 2015 Street Tree Census - Tree Data
  page_limit = 50000,          # SODA v2.0 max is 50,000; keep reasonable to avoid timeouts
  pause_sec  = 0.2,            # pause between requests (be polite)
  use_token  = TRUE            # if env var NYC_SODA_APP_TOKEN is set, send it
) {
  dir.create(dest_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  # Endpoints
  geojson_base <- glue("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/{base_id}.geojson")
  count_url    <- glue("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/{base_id}.json")

  # Optional app token (recommended if you have one to avoid throttling)
  app_token <- Sys.getenv("NYC_SODA_APP_TOKEN", unset = NA)

  # 1) Fetch total row count using a cheap JSON count query (fast + tiny payload)
  count_req <- request(count_url) |>
    req_url_query(`$select` = "count(1)")
  if (use_token && !is.na(app_token) && nzchar(app_token)) {
    count_req <- count_req |> req_headers(`X-App-Token` = app_token)
  }
  n_total <- count_req |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)
  if (!("count_1" %in% names(n_total))) stop("Count query did not return count(1).")
  n_total <- as.integer(n_total$count_1)

  message("Total rows reported by API: ", format(n_total, big.mark = ","))

  # 2) Iterate pages with $limit / $offset; save each page to data/mp03
  n_pages <- ceiling(n_total / page_limit)
  page_indices <- seq_len(n_pages)

  files <- map_chr(page_indices, function(i) {
    offset <- (i - 1) * page_limit
    fname  <- file.path(dest_dir, sprintf("treepoints_%s_limit%05d_offset%07d.geojson",
                                          base_id, page_limit, offset))
    if (file.exists(fname) && file.size(fname) > 0) {
      message("Reusing local file: ", basename(fname))
      return(fname)
    }

    # Build request for this page
    req <- request(geojson_base) |>
      req_url_query(`$limit` = page_limit, `$offset` = offset)

    if (use_token && !is.na(app_token) && nzchar(app_token)) {
      req <- req |> req_headers(`X-App-Token` = app_token)
    }

    # Perform and write to disk atomically
    resp <- req_perform(req)
    body <- resp_body_raw(resp)
    writeBin(body, fname)
    message("Downloaded: ", basename(fname))
    Sys.sleep(pause_sec)
    fname
  })

  # 3) Read all GeoJSON pages with sf::st_read and combine
  #    (sf will keep geometry column; attributes unioned by name)
  message("Reading ", length(files), " GeoJSON file(s) with sf::st_read ...")
  pieces <- map(files, ~ st_read(.x, quiet = TRUE))
  bind_rows(pieces)
}
```

```{r}
library(sf)
```

```{r}
# Assuming you already ran these:
# council_sf <- get_nyc_council_districts()
# trees_sf   <- get_nyc_tree_points()

# Spatial join: assign district to each tree
trees_with_districts <- st_join(
  trees_sf, 
  council_sf,
  join = st_intersects   # trees first → use st_intersects
)

# Inspect
trees_with_districts %>% 
  dplyr::select(tree_id = tree_id_fieldname_here, district = council_fieldname_here) %>% 
  head()
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

trees_per_district <- trees_with_districts %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%                        # drop geometry for speed
  count(council_district = coundist) %>%        # <-- replace “coundist” with your actual field name
  arrange(desc(n))

top_district <- trees_per_district %>% slice(1)
top_district
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# 1) Count trees per district (from the joined dataset)
trees_per_district <- trees_with_districts %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%                          # no geometry needed for counting
  count(district = coundist, name = "tree_count") # replace coundist with your field name

# 2) Extract district areas from the council shapes
district_areas <- council_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%                          # keep only attributes
  select(district = coundist, shape_area)         # shape_area is in square feet

# 3) Combine tree counts + district areas
density_df <- trees_per_district %>%
  left_join(district_areas, by = "district") %>%
  mutate(
    tree_density = tree_count / shape_area        # trees per sq ft
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(tree_density))

densest <- density_df %>% slice(1)
densest
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

dead_fraction <- trees_with_districts %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  # Replace "coundist" with your actual district column
  group_by(district = coundist) %>%
  summarize(
    total_trees = n(),
    dead_trees  = sum(health == "Dead", na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_dead   = dead_trees / total_trees
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(frac_dead))

dead_fraction %>% slice(1)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# ---- 1. Add borough column based on council district number ----
trees_borough <- trees_with_districts %>%
  mutate(
    borough = case_when(
      coundist >= 1  & coundist <= 10 ~ "Manhattan",
      coundist >= 11 & coundist <= 18 ~ "Bronx",
      coundist >= 19 & coundist <= 32 ~ "Queens",
      coundist >= 33 & coundist <= 48 ~ "Brooklyn",
      coundist >= 49 & coundist <= 51 ~ "Staten Island",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# ---- 2. Filter to Manhattan trees ----
manhattan_trees <- trees_borough %>%
  filter(borough == "Manhattan")

# ---- 3. Count species and extract the most common ----
common_species_manhattan <- manhattan_trees %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(spc_common)) %>%    # optional: drop missing species names
  count(spc_common, sort = TRUE)

# Print the full ranking
common_species_manhattan

# Most common species only
common_species_manhattan %>% slice(1)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# ---- 1. Helper function for creating a CRS-tagged point ----
new_st_point <- function(lat, lon){
  st_sfc(st_point(c(lon, lat))) |>   # IMPORTANT: (lon, lat) order
    st_set_crs("WGS84")
}

# ---- 2. Create Baruch point ----
baruch_pt <- new_st_point(
  lat = 40.7403,
  lon = -73.9830
)

# ---- 3. Compute distance to each tree ----
trees_with_distance <- trees_with_districts %>%
  mutate(
    distance_m = st_distance(geometry, baruch_pt) |> as.numeric()
  )

# ---- 4. Identify the closest tree ----
closest_tree <- trees_with_distance %>%
  slice_min(distance_m, n = 1)

closest_species <- closest_tree$spc_common
closest_species
```
